rows: Several cars were damaged by golf ball-size hail.
Trees down over the northern part of the county.
A tree was uprooted and fell on power lines. Garbage cans, lawn furniture, and tree limbs were also blown around.
Several tree branches were broken off.
Trees and a trailer were damaged.
Nickel-size hail was reported in Golinda.
Quarter-size hail was reported in the Reagan community.
A 70 MPH wind gust was reported southeast of Kosse.
A radio tower was snapped in half.
An 18 wheeler was blown over on HWY 77 and a tree was uprooted.
A mobile home was severely damaged, a grain bin was moved 100 yards, and a large tree and limbs were blown down by strong winds.
HAM radio operators estimated 60 mph thunderstorm outflow winds at the intersection of Highway 7 and County Road 439.
HAM radio operators reported golfball sized hail in Chilton.
Waco broadcast media reported nickel to golfball sized hail covering the ground 6 miles north of Lott along Highway 77.
HAM radio operators estimated thunderstorm outflow wind gusts up to 70 mph approximately 1 mile east of Belfalls.

A storm chaser caught a brief tornado approximately two miles south of Riesel. The tornado was on the ground as it crossed HWY 6, but otherwise the tornado remained over open land and did not cause any damage.
Quarter size hail was reported in Golinda.
Golf ball size hail was reported 4 miles south of Otto.
Quarter size hail covered the road about 3 miles southeast of Dott.
Penny size hail fell in Lott.
Quarter size hail covered the ground at the intersection of Highway 6 and Farm-to-Market Road 1373 south of Reagan.
Quarter size hail fell 1 mile south of Riesel on Highway 6.
A large tree was blown down east of Marlin.
Multiple trees were blown down in the town of Eloise.
Quarter sized hail was reported along FM 147 in northeastern Falls County.
Multiple trees were blown down across the county.
Law enforcement reported a tree being knocked over and was blocking the road near the intersection of Hwy 7 and CR 4012 in Chilton.
Law enforcement reported trees and power lines down just east of Marlin, TX.
Law enforcement reported trees down on several streets across town.
Falls County Sheriff's Department reported heavy wind damage along and east of Highway 6, approximately 3 miles southeast of Blue Ridge.
Newspaper article reported roof damage to residential structure approximated 4.6 miles SE in Reagan, TX.
Falls County Sheriff's Department reported trees and power lines down approximately one mile south of the city of Reagan, TX.
A social media report indicated tennis ball sized hail in the city of Eddy, TX.
A public report indicated ping pong sized hail approximately 6 miles south southwest of the city of Golinda, TX.
A public report indicated golf ball sized hail approximately 5 miles south of the city of Golinda, TX.
Falls County Sheriff's Department reported 10 to 12 inch diameter trees down on FM 147 approximately 1 mile north of the city of Marlin, TX.
Amateur radio reported a measured wind gust of 58 MPH by a home weather station near the city of Rosebud, TX.
Broadcast media reported quarter size hail in the city of Marlin, TX.
Hail ranging from 1.5 - 2 was reported in Marlin via multiple sources. Damage to vehicles was reported.
Snapped trees and downed trees were reported in Marlin via social media.
A barn roof was blown off. Time was estimated by radar.
A farmer reported crops were destroyed and a total loss. Time was estimated by radar.
Multiple trees and large branches were down near CR 1373 near State Highway 6. The winds were estimated at 70 mph. Time estimated by radar.
Golf ball size hail was reported west of Rosebud.
A trained spotter reported nickel to quarter sized hail near FM 1772 in Barclay.
A trained spotter reported hail up to quarter size near Wilson.

Egg size hail was reported 8 miles west of Rosebud.

Thunderstorm winds caused damage to power poles and power lines in the Rosebud area. Some damage to outbuildings and other structures was also reported. Wind driven hail may have also cracked and shattered windows, but no hail size could be obtained.
Strong winds in Barclay broke several power poles, causing a power outage in the community. In additional a large metal barn was nearly destroyed.
A trained spotter reported minor tree and powerline damage approximately 1 mile west of Rosebud, TX.

Amateur radio reported golf ball sized hail about 7 miles west-northwest of Rosebud, TX.
A public report indicated quarter sized hail in Rosebud, TX.
Amateur radio reported quarter sized hail about a mile north-northwest of Rosebud, TX.
A public report indicated tennis ball sized hail about 5 miles southwest of Rosebud, TX.

A narrow tornado was videoed in a field for 2-3 minutes. The exact location is unknown but is close to the plotted track. This tornado was the first of 4 brief tornadoes a parent supercell produced as it moved across Falls and Limestone counties.
Amateur radio reported nickel to quarter sized hail at 447 FM 1772 west of Rosebud, TX.
Amateur radio reported a wind gust of 78 MPH near Durango, TX.
Broadcast media reported damage to the roof and windows of a Dairy Queen on Highway 77 near Rosebud, and additional window damage near the center of town.
Amateur radio reported an 18 wheeler flipped, a 15-inch diameter tree snapped, and a camper trailer blown around 40 feet. A personal weather station (KTXROSEB15) reported a wind gust of 79 MPH.
A ham radio operator reported golf ball size hail on CR 478 in Durango.
Emergency Manager reports roof damage to multiple structures including a single family home near Durango, TX.
Broadcast media reported ping pong size hail in Cedar Spring.

Emergency management reported two-inch diameter hail on Highway 7 west of Kosse.
A public report contained a photo of the roof at the World Finance building in Marlin, TX collapsed.
Tree limbs and power lines were down.
